items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we are gathering from today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share their land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.

Recently, about two weeks ago, two Waterloo residents, Paul Born and Dr. Donna Strickland, were honoured with the Order of Canada, which is a tremendous honour and recognition for two residents in our community. We had invited them to come today to be recognized and to receive a certificate and our gratitude, however they were unfortunately not able to make it, so we will ask them if they can attend a Council meeting in January 2023 so that we can more formally recognize them and their achievements on behalf of our community. In their absence, we just want to extend our sincere congratulations to Paul Born and Dr. Donna Strickland for their incredible achievements.

notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
notes: That the previous meeting minutes be approved.

items.title: Consent Motion
notes: Councillor Bodaly requested that items 7 c) 2023 Building Standards Fees and Charges and 7 d) Rental Housing and Business Licensing Fees and Charges 2023 be removed from the consent motion.
That consent motion items (a) through (c) be approved.

items.title: Items Removed From the Consent Motion
2023 Building Standards Fees and Charges
notes: Beth Maxwell responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Rental Housing and Business Licensing
notes: Nicole Papke responded to questions of Council. Kim Reger also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: 2023 Proposed Budget – Summary:
notes: Mayor McCabe offered some introductory remarks, noting that the budget is the main tool that will allow Council to implement the Strategic Plan and allow staff to deliver programs and services to the community.
Councillor Freeman offered further introductory remarks, noting that the budget is a monumental task of finding balance, and we are living in challenging economic times.

Filipa Reynolds & Brad Witzel delivered a presentation on the highlights of the proposed budget. They touched on the budget goals, the link to the strategic plan, and the breakdown of the proposed budget. They further detailed the Capital Budget program and the key budget documents.

items.title: Reserves and Reserve Funds Annual Update
notes: Julie Koppeser gave a presentation outlining Reserves and Reserve Funds, their differences and uses, and the impacts on them by Development Charges.

items.title: City Utilities – 2023 Rates
notes: Leigh McDermott and Michael Pugliese gave a presentation on the rate setting objectives, how the rates are distributed, how Waterloo’s rate increases compare to surrounding municipalities, and a detailed look at the reserve funding. They then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Uptown CIP Update
notes: Joseph Segato gave a presentation providing an update on Community Improvement Plan, including some examples of the façade improvement grant. He then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Bill 23: More Homes Built Faster Act,
notes: Prepared By: Joel Cotter and Filipa Reynolds

Joel Cotter and Filipa Reynolds delivered a presentation providing context to Bill 23, outlining planning and financial considerations, and how the City plans to adapt to the new legislation. They then responded to questions of Council.

Kae Elgie, Resident of Waterloo, gave a brief presentation offering thanks to the City and Council for their quick response, as well as showcasing how the public has responded to the passing of Bill 23. She then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Vasic wanted to shout out “Light Up Lincoln Heights” occurring in the Lincoln Heights neighbourhood again this year, where many houses are already lit up, and there’s a contest for decorating.

motions.item_title: Reserves and Reserve Funds Annual Update
motions.text: 1. That Council approve report CORP2022-049. 2. That Council approve the Community Benefits Charge Reserve Fund Policy attached as Appendix A. 3. That Council approve the Climate Action Reserve Fund Policy attached as Appendix B. 4. That Council approve that the Green Initiatives program within CRF be closed and the balance transferred to the Climate Action Reserve Fund. 5. That Council approve that $918,000 of the annual CRF funding allocation be redirected as a permanent source of funding for the Climate Action Reserve Fund. 6. That Council approve that the Library program within CIRRF be closed and the balance transferred to the Library Expansion Reserve Fund. 7. That Council approve the following administrative adjustment be updated in the Reserves and Reserve Funds Policies: a. That Council approve that the Parking Reserve Fund City Maintenance program be renamed to the City Parking Infrastructure program to better align with the mainly capital nature of the expenditures. 8. That Council approve that FC-006 Reserves and Reserve Funds Policy, attached as Appendix D, be updated for the changes required through recommendations 1 through 7, inclusive.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approve report CORP2022-049.

2. That Council approve the Community Benefits Charge Reserve Fund Policy attached as Appendix A.

3. That Council approve the Climate Action Reserve Fund Policy attached as Appendix B.

4. That Council approve that the Green Initiatives program within CRF be closed and the balance transferred to the Climate Action Reserve Fund.

5. That Council approve that $918,000 of the annual CRF funding allocation be redirected as a permanent source of funding for the Climate Action Reserve Fund.

6. That Council approve that the Library program within CIRRF be closed and the balance transferred to the Library Expansion Reserve Fund.

7. That Council approve the following administrative adjustment be updated in the Reserves and Reserve Funds Policies: a. That Council approve that the Parking Reserve Fund City Maintenance program be renamed to the City Parking Infrastructure program to better align with the mainly capital nature of the expenditures.

8. That Council approve that FC-006 Reserves and Reserve Funds Policy, attached as Appendix D, be updated for the changes required through recommendations 1 through 7, inclusive.
